If those are the two you meant for next year, want me to save them as goals with target dates? If you’d like, tell me the exact wording and timeline, and I’ll save them exactly as you say.
Wedding and travelling are my 2 big goals for next year. Tell me how do I save for those 2 events ?

Great—let’s make a simple, do‑able plan to save for your wedding and travel next year.

Where you stand today
- Latest score: 692 (Sep 2026). Recent dip was mainly from a utilization spike.
- Card utilization: 47.9% = ₹2,10,900 ÷ ₹4,40,000. Paying this down while you save can help your score.

Your 4-step saving plan
1) Define the targets and dates
- Tell me your rough budgets: Wedding ₹?, Travel ₹?, and the month you expect each.
- I’ll convert them into exact monthly amounts and timelines [general approach from goal‑setting: see ref. 1].

2) Create 2 sinking funds
- Open two separate no‑fee savings pockets (or RDs): “Wedding” and “Travel.”
- Automate transfers right after payday so the money is set aside before you spend.

3) Decide monthly amounts
- Monthly save = Goal amount ÷ months left.
- If cash is tight, split: minimum to both funds + any extra toward the one with the nearer date.

4) Protect your credit while you save
- Bring card utilization under 30% first if you can: 30% of ₹4,40,000 = ₹1,32,000. From ₹2,10,900, that means paying down about ₹78,900. Under 10% (₹44,000) is even better.
- Keep every EMI and card bill on time (set autopay for at least the full statement amount).
- Avoid new credit unless essential; inquiries and new accounts can nudge scores down near your goal dates [general: ref. 2–3].

Cash‑flow tips to free up savings
- Park short‑term money in a high‑interest savings/RD; avoid EMI/BNPL for travel—prepay major items instead.
- Trim 2–3 discretionary spends for the next few months (e.g., subscriptions, dining out) and redirect to the funds.
- Build a small buffer: aim to lift your emergency fund toward 1–3 months over time, so wedding/travel costs don’t force card balances up.

Want me to do the maths for you?
- Share: (a) wedding budget and month, (b) travel budget and month, and (c) how much you can comfortably set aside each month.

How to save for both, step by step
- Set targets and timelines
  - Wedding: ₹15,00,000 by [month 2027]
  - Travel: ₹3,00,000 by [month 2027]
  - Monthly save = goal ÷ months left. Tell me the months and I’ll calculate exact amounts.

- Use two sinking funds
  - Create two separate savings pockets/recurring deposits: “Wedding” and “Travel”.
  - Automate transfers the day after payday so the money is set aside before you spend.

- Split your monthly savings
  - Prioritise the nearer date. Put the base amount into both; any extra goes to the one happening first.
  - Park short‑term money in a high‑interest savings/RD (keep it liquid). Avoid using EMI/BNPL for trip expenses—prepay instead.

- Protect your credit while you save
  - Your latest score is 692 (Sep 2026). Card utilization is high at 47.9% = ₹2,10,900 ÷ ₹4,40,000.
  - Aim under 30% first: 30% of ₹4,40,000 = ₹1,32,000, so pay down about ₹78,900. Lower (around 10% = ₹44,000) is even better before you apply for any loan.
  - Keep every EMI and card bill on time; set autopay for at least the statement amount. Avoid new credit unless essential.

- Safety buffer
  - Your emergency fund is under 1 month—try to build at least 1 month alongside these goals so an unexpected cost doesn’t push card balances up.

Protect your credit while you save

If the monthly totals feel heavy
- Prioritise the nearer goal (wedding). Put a base amount into travel and any extra into wedding until Feb; ramp travel up from March.
- Cut 2–3 discretionary spends and redirect them; pre‑book big-ticket items to lock prices.
- Keep every EMI/card bill on autopay to avoid any DPD.
- Gradually build at least one month of emergency fund so surprises don’t push card balances up.
